recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source edit is needed for FHIR-32578 unless OO later decides to split DocumentReference.type away from the shared doc-typecodes value set through a new issue.
issue_request: FHIR-32578 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO change request for R5 asking that the DocumentReference document type binding not be limited to the earlier narrow document-type set; the resolution was to change the example set to the doc-typecodes value set already used by Composition.
initial_application: The relevant source history first changed DocumentReference.type from DocumentC80Type/ValueSet/c80-doc-typecodes to DocumentType/ValueSet/doc-typecodes in cebeac615e0c434ff755a1aa763781d2cf61c8c2. The explicit FHIR-32578 commit 63e34f95aa90a1abb55f7221d0e450049e9342d3 briefly changed the binding strength to example, but ca285c8a45fd6e2f997ebbf7e52f974e24e80f00 restored preferred strength before the Jira-commented merge 333a55c82177c6a441312c2153b3d7a6abe8a507 landed.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists composition and documentreference as active resources. Related combined-branch audits for FHIR-32822 and FHIR-28078 show the same binding family: FHIR-32822 coordinated the non-C80 DocumentReference type binding with FHIR-32578, and later FHIR-28078 explicitly records doc-typecodes as applied as a preferred binding to DocumentReference.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because current DocumentReference.type and Composition.type both use http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/doc-typecodes. The separate source/documentreference/valueset-doc-typecodes.xml artifact is not the binding target of DocumentReference.type and was left unchanged.
